the question: what kind of cultural identity is constructed in Chinese history textbooks? The results show that the textbooks construct an exclusive Chinese identity that is based on the Han majority culture.
the question of how multiculturalism is constructed in Hong Kong Chinese historical narratives, and how these narratives can be used to promote multicultural education in Hong Kong.

, although Hong Kong Chinese history curricula are designed to be multicultural, the content of the textbooks is not.
the Chinese History textbooks in Hong Kong do not provide a multicultural approach to history.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the history textbooks in Hong Kong do not provide a balanced and multicultural perspective on the relationship between majority and minority cultures.
multiculturalism has not yet been established as an important value in Hong Kong Chinese identity.
the current Chinese history curriculum and textbooks in Hong Kong do not support multicultural education aims.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multicultural content in history education should be more than a descriptive exercise.
multicultural content in history textbooks in Hong Kong needs to be more inclusive and balanced in order to support a multicultural society in Hong Kong.
multicultural content should not just be included in textbooks but also be represented in a way that supports the aims of multiculturalism.
